experiment_template.research_question: Can a compact terminal decision state replace repeated review scaffolding, improve GLM-5.3-flash context selection at 8K, and use no more cumulative tokens than control?
stop_conditions: Any unbounded unknown usage, retry, asymmetric score, integrity failure, or cost-cap violation stops before the next task.
Stop immediately when six eligible pairs become mathematically unreachable.

records.falsifier: Fewer than six pairs are eligible, any boundary or ancestry proof fails, treatment first-request input is not at least 128 tokens lower in every causal pair, treatment aggregate tokens exceed control, any quality metric degrades, or macro Span-F1 gain is below 0.05.
records.mechanism: Fork only at the first held terminal candidate. Control retains the existing neutral review; treatment substitutes one decision-state/v2 record for the verbose held-candidate review and repeated finalization messages.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash fresh scoreable 8K ContextBench development tasks at the 96K cumulative input-plus-output tier.
records.statement: A compact terminal decision state can replace repeated review scaffolding, preserve the terminal quality signal, and reduce first-request input tokens.
